content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity) — § 2.2 exclusivity binding Customer.**

- **Issue:** § 2.2 makes Vendor our "sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term" — full-term exclusive dealing with no category limit, no 12-month cap, and no exit on SLA or delivery failure. This fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory.
- **Internal conflict:** § 12.3 has Vendor acknowledge that Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." There is no order-of-precedence clause in the document, so the two provisions are irreconcilable as drafted.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** § 2.2 is recast so Vendor is *a* provider, with express confirmation that we owe no minimum volume and may source analytics or other services from third parties at any time — consistent with § 12.3.
- **Negotiation room noted:** if Vendor resists deletion, the outer limit is the fallback — one defined product category, 12 months, terminating automatically on any service-level or delivery failure.
